pageCache.text:
Welcome to Winterbourne Junior Girls’ School
I would like to welcome you to Winterbourne Junior Girls’ School. Through this prospectus, I hope to give you a glimpse of our school, of our ethos, our values and the vision we have for the girls in our care. There is a strong focus on raising pupils’ aspirations.
Key Information
Click on the heading to view some key information.
Testimonials
Click on the heading to read what they say about our school.
Parents Links
Click on the heading to access all key information for parents.
News/Events
Click on the heading to view our latest news and events.
ADMISSIONS
ADMISSIONS
Click on the link below for more information.

POLICIES

ONLINE SAFETY

What they say about us
Leaders support pupils to learn about their own identities, interests and talents. One pupil said, reflecting the views of many, ‘School makes everyone feel unique and special. You feel like you belong here.’
This is a kind school where pupils are encouraged to accept others for who they are. Pupils listen carefully to each other and demonstrate respect for others’ views and experiences.
Pupils make good use of the worry boxes which are in all corridors and classrooms, as well as the ‘no worries booth’ in the playground where they can talk with a member of staff.
Teachers use their strong subject knowledge to explain new ideas clearly. They teach pupils the subject-specific vocabulary they need to talk about their learning accurately and in detail.
Pupils are well cared for. They have positive relationships with their teachers and other adults in the school who notice when something is wrong and take action to help them.
The School is a fantastic school with a wonderful ethos and community spirit. My daughters have been positively impacted by the amazing staff and a caring environment which has really shaped some of the most crucial years in their childhood. As parents, we also feel extremely supported by the school. Thank you!
Great school, great teachers and support. Lovely staff, amazing, good school. Daughter has made brilliant progress. My daughter loves school and talks about her teaching and learning at home.
I feel Winterbourne Junior Girls school is very good because they encourage students to work hard and teach them very well.
This school is one of the best schools. They take the learning and discipline very seriously and make constant improvements. They have created a very healthy environment for girls to grow and learn in the best way possible. Even though this school is far away from our home, we still drive 20-30 minutes just so our daughter attends it.
Very nice school. My daughter loves it! A nice place to be and for me and my daughter, the best school in the world!

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteachers Welcome – Winterbourne Junior Girls' School
pageCache.text:
Dear Parents and Carers,
I would like to welcome you to Winterbourne Junior Girls’ School. Through this prospectus, I hope to give you a glimpse of our school, of our ethos, our values and the vision we have for the girls in our care. There is a strong focus on raising pupils’ aspirations. This is central to the school’s aims and the headteacher’s vision (Ofsted 2015)
Our vision is centred on three fundamental goals:
It is my belief that these areas will enable us to improve our standards.
I believe that education is about developing the whole person: socially, emotionally, spiritually as well as academically. My aim is for us to work together to ensure that Winterbourne Junior Girls’ school provides excellent teaching and learning experiences in a happy and caring environment. By working together we can ensure that our girls enjoy their time here, make rapid progress and leave school equipped with the skills for lifelong learning. My expectations of the pupils, in terms of their achievement and behaviour, are very high.
I expect all members of the school community to uphold our values. I am sure you will agree that the girls’ ability to be successful in their learning is paramount and I am confident that you will support us in helping our girls to reach their goals. Our commitment to you is that, your daughter will be welcomed to Winterbourne Junior Girls’ School and leave with a broad and balanced breadth of knowledge and experience, ready to embrace the challenges of secondary school.
I look forward to meeting you and welcoming you to our school.
Aspirations,
Expectations,
Yours sincerely
Mrs M Berkeley-Agyepong Headteacher

Our School Values
We are interested in three kinds of outcomes for our girls:
Our chosen school values help to develop specific desirable characteristics in our girls.
Skills—what our students are able to do
Knowledge—what they know
Character—the kind of people they become
Our School Values are:
All of our values uphold British Values.
RESPECT
TOLERANCE
SELF (self-esteem, self-reliance, self-respect)
AMBITION
RESPONSIBILITY
FORGIVENESS
TEAM WORK
HONESTY
HARD WORK
INDEPENDENCE

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Vision statement – Winterbourne Junior Girls' School
pageCache.text:
Our Vision Statement
Winterbourne Junior Girls’ School aims to provide children the opportunity to develop towards their full potential; academically, emotionally and socially by encouraging a positive approach to all aspects of school life; creating a safe, caring and stimulating learning environment for all.
ACHIEVEMENT – to give everyone equal access to a broad and balanced education so they can realise their full potential.
SELF – to develop in everyone a sense of self-esteem, independence, enjoyment and co-operation.
INVOLVEMENT– to involve pupils and all adults associated with the school, in our organisation and discipline through clear communication.
RESPECT – to have respect for and courtesy towards others, recognising and being mindful of the protected characteristics as laid out in the Equality Act 2010 i.e. race; age; sex; religion or belief; disability; gender reassignment; marriage and civil partnership; pregnancy and maternity; sexual orientation
We carry these aims out through our ethos of: Aspirations, Expectations, No Excuses

pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care – Winterbourne Junior Girls' School
pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club (FREE OF CHARGE):
Breakfast clubs runs from Monday until Friday every morning starting at 07:30am – 08:30am.
Menu: Cereals, toast with butter or jam, eggs, pancakes, yoghurts etc…
The children enjoy lots of fun activities, games and craft time during the hour with Ms Sholay and Mrs Rahim who supervise the period each day.
Download an application form:
To download an application form, please click on the link below.
Breakfast-Club-Application-form
After School Care fees and times after an extra-curricular club:
Please use this link to book After School Care: https://forms.gle/zEnDzgBz9F9LbwUTA
Booking and payment in advance is required as we have to ensure we have enough staff cover. Arrears are not allowed. We regret that non-payment of fees will mean your daughter cannot attend additional services with immediate effect.
After School Care fees can be paid at www.parentpay.com. Please ask the School office if you do not have ParentPay account and login. We do not take cash. All parents must collect their children on time.
A charge will be made for any late collections: £5 for the first five minutes followed by an additional charge of £5 every five minutes (or part period of five minutes thereafter).
We will refund fees for any days when School is closed due to any emergency e.g. heating breakdown.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Opening Hours – Winterbourne Junior Girls' School
pageCache.text:
SCHOOL OPENING HOURS
At 8.30am the gates are opened so that the girls can enter the playground (please note the girls are unsupervised until 8.45am). At 8.45am the girls will be escorted by their class TA from the playground to their classrooms and given time to get ready for the school day.
The playground door will be shut promptly at 9am. Late comers are to enter through the main entrance (front of school).
School Session Times:
The school day is broken into various teaching sessions.
Pupils are escorted off the playground and into class
Registration and Early Morning Work
Year 3 Class Dismissal
Year 4 Class Dismissal
Year 5 Class Dismissal
Year 6 Class Dismissal
Breakfast Club runs from 7:30am. After School Clubs run from clubs 3.45-4.45pm.
Collection Times:
Year 3: 3.30pm – Year 4: 3.30pm – Year 5: 3.35pm – Year 6 3.40pm
Children must be collected from the playground, not at/outside the gate or any other location. If you or person in charge of your child is running late or there is a change to your usual arrangement please let us know as soon as possible before 3pm by calling the office on 020 8684 3532. It is extremely difficult to pass messages to children once they are out of class.
Travelling home alone:
Children are able to travel home alone, or with older siblings if you give permission. A form is available from the office.
Mobile phones:
If your daughter does require a mobile phone when travelling home alone, please complete a form in the office. Mobile phones are kept in the School office and must not be kept in your daughter’s bag or pockets.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maths Planner – Winterbourne Junior Girls' School
pageCache.text:
Maths Planner
At Winterbourne Junior Girls’ School, we aim to deliver a stimulating, high quality curriculum with a strong emphasis on the basic skills and knowledge, which will prepare the children well for their future. At the same time, we aim to instil in the children a life-long love of learning.
We provide Quality First Teaching, using a mastery approach for Maths, which focuses on small steps and formative assessment to ensure that all pupils have fully grasped a concept before moving on or deepening learning. We aim to make learning a rewarding and enjoyable experience by providing a range of activities and opportunities for using concrete and pictorial resources before consolidating using abstract concepts. Ensuring that all pupils are engaged and able to access tasks at greater depth, leads to good learning behaviour and enables all pupils to reach their full potential.
Maths Mastery utilises the five Big Ideas of Maths:
These are in line with the National Programmes of Study for Maths, which emphasise fluency, coherence, variation in representation and the development of increasingly sophisticated problem-solving skills.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Governors – Winterbourne Junior Girls' School
pageCache.text:
Governors of Winterbourne Junior Girls’ School
The Governing Body is constituted by an ‘Instrument of Government’ as defined and required by the Government. The Instrument sets out the categories, numbers and terms of office of governors:
Co-opted governors; as determined by the governing body and no more than 1/3 where they are also eligible to be elected as staff governors when counted with the staff governor and Head Teacher.
The Governing Body sets the strategic direction, the vision and the ethos of the school. In doing so it has a number of key responsibilities:
The purpose of maintained school governing bodies is to ‘conduct the school with a view to promoting high standards of educational achievement at the school. This is achieved through:
The governors carry out these functions through its termly full meetings, visits to the school and the work of its two principal working parties:
Other committees are put together to deal with other functions including the Pay Review Appeal committee (PPA), The Way Forward committee (WFC) and the Headteachers Performance and Salary Review committee (HTPSR).
Governors, along with staff members, who regularly attend meetings of the Governing Body and its working parties must declare any business or personal interest that might influence any decision they may make especially in financial matters. Any governor with such an interest must declare it annually and notify the school of any changes that occur. Where there is a conflict of interest the governor must withdraw from the meeting and take no part in the discussions or vote. The agenda of each meeting requires governors and non-governors present to declare any interest they may have in any of the items to be discussed.

This week, Year 5 visited the Science Museum as part of their Science Topic on DNA and the Human Body. They became real scientists for the day as they studied the method of extracting DNA from a banana, learning more about the human body and what we put into them.
